candidates.text: Under the doctrine of Meyer v. Nebraska, 262 U. S. 390, we think it entirely plain that the Act of 1922 unreasonably interferes with the liberty of parents and guardians
candidates.speaker: McReynolds, J.
phrases: liberty of parents and guardians to direct the upbringing and education of children under their control

candidates.text: The fundamental theory of liberty upon which all governments in this Union repose excludes any general power of the State to standardize its children
candidates.speaker: McReynolds, J.
phrases: The child is not the mere creature of the State
standardize its children by forcing them to accept instruction from public teachers only

candidates.text: No question is raised concerning the power of the State reasonably to regulate all schools, to inspect, supervise and examine them
candidates.speaker: McReynolds, J.
phrases: power of the State reasonably to regulate all schools, to inspect, supervise and examine them

candidates.text: Plaintiffs asked protection against arbitrary, unreasonable and unlawful interference with their patrons
candidates.speaker: McReynolds, J.
